meta.title: Python SDK · {brand}
meta.description: The Python SDK on the shared Rust core: install from source, authenticate, a first script, and which SDK call reaches each v1 endpoint. In development; not published yet.

heading: Python SDK.
lede: An idiomatic Python layer on the shared Rust core nf-core (PyO3, abi3 for Python 3.12 and later). Hashing, canonical JSON, retries, the encrypted stream buffer and the offline provenance recorder run in the core.
source: bindings/python/README.md; the code blocks are named under each block.

sections.heading: Status
body: The SDK is in development and not published to a package index. Its API can still change.
Release wheels (abi3; Windows, macOS and Linux) are built in CI by a manually started workflow that has no publish step. Each release will state its end-of-support date.
Nothing in this package sends anything to acquisition hardware.

sections.heading: What is in it
body: Optional extras: {pkg}[stream] (grpcio) for streaming, {pkg}[lsl] (pylsl) for the LSL inlet bridge, {pkg}[mne] (MNE-Python) for MNE interop.

items.heading: nf.open, nf.recordings
items.body: Local files, hashed on your machine, and platform recordings (read, to_mne).

items.heading: nf.pipelines
items.body: get(ref), publish(spec), Pipeline.run(rec). The pipeline ID is recomputed locally.

items.heading: nf.runs
items.body: Run.wait(), Run.record, Run.provenance with lineage() and export("prov-json").

items.heading: nf.streaming
items.body: Device keys, open_stream, Stream.push, run_acquisition (stream extra).

items.heading: nf.lsl
items.body: LSL inlet bridge that records clock offsets (lsl extra).

items.heading: nf.local
items.body: Offline provenance recorder, Zarr v3 nf-signal/1 store, chunk cache.

sections.heading: Build from source
body: Until wheels are published, build a debug version of the package from a source checkout with maturin and run its tests. These are the development commands of the SDK README (Windows paths).

sections.heading: Authenticate and configure
body: nf.configure(api_url=..., token=..., session=...) sets the client that nf.open, nf.pipelines and the other modules use, and returns it as an nf.Client. Without it, the client reads NF_API_URL, NF_API_TOKEN and NF_SESSION from the environment; streaming also reads NF_INGEST_TARGET, the host and port of the ingest service.
The token is an API key or an access token, sent as a bearer credential. Pass refresh=, a function that returns a new token, and the client calls it once after a 401 response.
There is no hosted service yet; the quickstarts run against a local test instance with demo data.

sections.heading: A first script
body: Resolve a pinned pipeline version. The SDK recomputes its content ID from the steps, images, parameters and seed, so a version cannot change under its name. This block is the first step of the pipeline-run quickstart and runs in CI.

sections.heading: Run it on a recording
body: run uploads a local file first, queues the pipeline and returns at once; wait polls until the run ends and raises if it failed. Errors from the API are RFC 9457 problem documents, raised as NfApiError.
Source: bindings/python/python/{pkg}/pipelines.py (Pipeline.run) and runs.py (Run.wait); errors in client.py (NfApiError).

endpoints.heading: One call per v1 endpoint
body: Every operation of the v1 API reference, with the SDK function that calls it. Operations without a wrapper yet are reached through the configured client: nf.get_client() returns it, and its get, post and request methods add the credentials, retry idempotent requests and raise problem documents as NfApiError.
This table is checked against the SDK source: each named function exists and contains the call to its endpoint.
Source: bindings/python/python/{pkg}/ (the file named for each wrapper in the test) and openapi/v1.yaml.
